questions.prompt: Which sentence uses principal correctly to mean chief or main?
choices: The principle concern was whether the trail remained safe.
The principal concern was whether the trail remained safe.
The principals concern was whether the trail remained safe.
The principle's concern was whether the trail remained safe.
questions.explanation: Principal is the adjective that means chief or main.

questions.prompt: According to the AP Stylebook, which spelling is preferred for the general term for a site on the World Wide Web?
choices: websites
web site
web-site
website
questions.explanation: The AP Stylebook treats website as a single word.

questions.prompt: Which sentence follows the traditional rule for using "whom" as an object?
choices: Whom did you give the book to?
Who did you give the book to?
Who gave the book to you?
Whom gave the book to you?
questions.explanation: "Whom" is the object of the preposition "to" in the clause.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a comma before a coordinating conjunction joining three independent clauses?
choices: The bus was late, the rain stopped, and the team arrived on time.
The bus was late the rain stopped and the team arrived on time.
The bus was late; the rain stopped and the team arrived on time.
The bus was late, the rain stopped; and the team arrived on time.
questions.explanation: When three independent clauses form a series, the first two are separated by commas and a comma appears before and.
questions.skill: Punctuating a series of independent clauses

questions.prompt: A publication's style guide says to use different from rather than different than. Which sentence follows that rule?
choices: The route was differed from the one we took yesterday.
The route was different than the one we took yesterday.
The route was differ from the one we took yesterday.
The route was different from the one we took yesterday.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses different from, matching the construction required by the style guide.
questions.skill: Applying a style guide's preference between similar constructions

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an infinitive correctly to express purpose?
choices: She crossed the finish line by celebrate her victory.
She crossed the finish line for celebrate her victory.
She crossed the finish line in order celebrating her victory.
She crossed the finish line to celebrate her victory.
questions.explanation: An infinitive expresses purpose and takes the form of to followed by a verb.

questions.prompt: A style guide says to place a comma after an introductory dependent clause beginning with After. Which sentence follows that rule?
choices: After the debate ended, the panel announced the winner.
After the debate ended the panel announced the winner.
After the debate ended, the panel, announced the winner.
After the debate ended the panel, announced the winner.
questions.explanation: The introductory dependent clause After the debate ended is followed by a comma before the main clause.

questions.prompt: A legal-drafting style guide says to use shall for duties imposed by a contract. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The tenant shall paying rent on the first day of each month.
The tenant shall to pay rent on the first day of each month.
The tenant shall pay rent on the first day of each month.
The tenant shall pays rent on the first day of each month.
questions.explanation: The sentence correctly uses shall to state a contractual duty without an additional verb form.

questions.prompt: A style guide says to spell out numbers below 10 but use numerals for 10 and above. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The workshop registered 12 teams and used four stations.
The workshop registered twelve teams and used four stations.
The workshop registered 12 teams and used 4 stations.
The workshop registered twelve teams and used 10 stations.
questions.explanation: The option uses the numeral 12 for a number above 10 and spells out four because it is below 10.

questions.prompt: A research center's style guide treats data as a mass noun. Which sentence follows that rule?
choices: The team collected datas before the survey closed.
The team collected a data before the survey closed.
The team collected data before the survey closed.
The team collected a datum before the survey closed.
questions.explanation: Data functions as one mass noun here, so it takes neither an article nor a plural ending.
questions.skill: Applying a style guide's treatment of data

questions.prompt: According to traditional style-guide guidance, which sentence correctly uses which for a nonrestrictive clause?
choices: The car that parked outside was red.
The book, which I borrowed, was overdue.
The house that has a blue door is for sale.
The book that I borrowed was overdue.
questions.explanation: The book, which I borrowed, was overdue uses which for a nonrestrictive clause, as traditional style-guide guidance recommends.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly to join two independent clauses?
choices: The library opens at eight; the cafe closes at six.
The library opens at eight; after the cafe closes at six.
The library opens at eight; the cafe that closes at six.
The library opens at eight; beside the cafe closes at six.
questions.explanation: A semicolon can join two independent clauses, as it does between the two complete clauses in the first sentence.

questions.prompt: Which possessive form correctly shows that multiple workers jointly own the equipment?
choices: workers equipment
worker's equipment
workers' equipment
workers's equipment
questions.explanation: A plural possessive takes an apostrophe after the plural noun, making workers' the correct form before equipment.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses that to introduce a restrictive clause?
choices: The bike, that I repaired, won the race.
The bike that I repaired won the race.
The bike which I repaired won the race.
The bike, which I repaired, won the race.
questions.explanation: The clause that I repaired identifies a particular bike and therefore should not be separated from the noun by commas.

questions.prompt: A writer faces two reputable style guides that recommend different treatments for the same document. What is the best response?
choices: Search for whichever rule receives the most online votes.
Ask which style guide the editor or publisher has designated.
Apply the stricter rule whenever two guides conflict.
Choose the guide with the larger number of pages.
questions.explanation: Choosing the guide designated by the editor or publisher establishes whose language conventions apply to the document.

questions.prompt: According to the AP Stylebook, which sentence correctly formats a quotation within a quotation?
choices: The writer called it “a minor ‘problem’.”
The writer called it ‘a “minor” problem.’
The writer called it “a ‘minor problem’.”
The writer called it “a ‘minor’ problem.”
questions.explanation: AP style uses double quotation marks for the outer quotation and single quotation marks for the quotation within it.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses than correctly in a comparison?
choices: The second lap was faster than the first.
The second lap was faster then the first.
The second lap was more fast than the first.
The second lap was fast than the first.
questions.explanation: Than is the preposition used to introduce the second element of a comparison.

questions.prompt: According to the Chicago Manual of Style, which sentence uses the serial comma correctly?
choices: The debate covered grammar, punctuation and documentation.
The debate covered grammar punctuation and documentation.
The debate covered grammar, punctuation, and documentation.
The debate covered grammar punctuation, and documentation.
questions.explanation: Chicago style recommends a comma before and in a series of three or more items.
questions.skill: Applying Chicago Manual of Style punctuation

questions.prompt: According to the AP Stylebook, which sentence uses an em dash with the correct spacing?
choices: The forecast–although surprising–held.
The forecast — although surprising — held.
The forecast—although surprising—held.
The forecast – although surprising – held.
questions.explanation: AP style uses an em dash without spaces on both sides for a parenthetical interruption.

questions.prompt: Which sentence applies subject-verb agreement correctly when the subject is the number of tickets sold?
choices: The number of tickets sold has increased this year.
The number of tickets sold have increased this year.
The number of tickets sold are increasing this year.
The number of tickets sold been increasing this year.
questions.explanation: The singular noun number is the subject, so it takes the singular verb has even when the phrase of tickets sold follows it.

questions.prompt: A style guide says to spell out an unfamiliar abbreviation on first use, followed by the abbreviation in parentheses. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The club joined the Bicycle Transportation Association and later referred to the BTA.
The club joined the (BTA) Bicycle Transportation Association to support safer routes.
The club joined the Bicycle Transportation Association (BTA for bicycles) to support safer routes.
The club joined the Bicycle Transportation Association (BTA) to support safer routes.
questions.explanation: The option spells out Bicycle Transportation Association on first use and then places its abbreviation BTA in parentheses.

questions.prompt: According to APA 7th edition, which parenthetical citation correctly refers to a work by three or more authors?
choices: (Smith, Lee, and Chen, 2020)
(Smith, 2020)
(Smith and Lee, 2020)
(Smith et al., 2020)
questions.explanation: APA 7th edition uses et al. in a parenthetical citation for a work with three or more authors.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the verb affect correctly?
choices: The delay may affected the results.
The delay may affects the results.
The delay may affect the results.
The delay may affecting the results.
questions.explanation: Affect is a verb meaning to influence, so it takes the base form may affect after a modal verb.
questions.topic: Timed Try 1: Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide asks writers to prefer active voice in ordinary narration. Which sentence uses active voice?
choices: The chain was tightened by the mechanic before the rider returned.
The mechanic tightened the chain before the rider returned.
The chain was being tightened by the mechanic before the rider returned.
The chain had been tightened by the mechanic before the rider returned.
questions.explanation: The option makes the mechanic the grammatical subject performing the action of tightening the chain.

questions.prompt: A style guide says to use a colon after a complete introductory clause when it introduces an explanation. Which sentence follows that rule?
choices: The cause was simple: the river had flooded the track.
The cause was simple; the river had flooded the track.
The cause was simple, and the river had flooded the track.
The cause was simple, the river had flooded the track.
questions.explanation: The colon correctly follows the complete introductory clause and introduces the explanation about the flooded river.
questions.skill: Using a colon to introduce an explanation

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses fewer correctly in a comparison?
choices: She has fewer apple than oranges.
She has less apples than oranges.
She has fewest apples than oranges.
She has fewer apples than oranges.
questions.explanation: Fewer modifies countable plural nouns such as apples, so fewer apples is the correct comparison.

questions.prompt: Which pronoun correctly completes this sentence: The student ___ submitted the report is available for questions?
choices: whom
who
whose
which
questions.explanation: Who is correct because it serves as the subject of the verb submitted.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly hyphenates the adjective before the noun?
choices: The director gave a well-reason response.
The director gave a well reasoned response.
The director gave a well-reasoned response.
The director gave a reason-well response.
questions.explanation: A hyphen joins the words in a compound adjective when the adjective appears before the noun it modifies.

questions.prompt: According to MLA 9th edition, how should a quotation longer than four lines of a source be formatted?
choices: In the paragraph inside quotation marks, single-spaced
On a new line without quotation marks, double-spaced
At the end of the paragraph in parentheses, double-spaced
In a footnote inside quotation marks, single-spaced
questions.explanation: MLA 9th edition places a long quotation on a new line without quotation marks and double-spaces it.
questions.skill: Formatting a quotation according to MLA style

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a colon to introduce a list of related items?
choices: The workshop offered three supplies, notebooks pens and folders.
The workshop offered three supplies; notebooks, pens, and folders.
The workshop offered three supplies: notebooks pens and folders.
The workshop offered three supplies: notebooks, pens, and folders.
questions.explanation: A colon correctly introduces the list, and commas separate the three items in the list.

questions.prompt: Which pair of words correctly completes the sentence? Yesterday the parcel ___ on the porch, and today the dog ___ it down.
choices: lay, lay
laid, laid
lay, laid
lie, laid
questions.explanation: Lay is the past tense of lie, while laid is the past tense and past participle of lay.

questions.prompt: A style guide says that the plural form of criterion is criteria. Which sentence uses the word correctly?
choices: The short stories met three criterias for the contest.
The short stories met three criterion for the contest.
The short stories met three criterions for the contest.
The short stories met three criteria for the contest.
questions.explanation: Because criteria is the plural of criterion, three criteria is the correctly formed phrase.
questions.skill: Applying plural forms from a style guide

questions.prompt: A style guide recommends using due to to express a cause. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The race was delayed due to heavy rain.
The race was delayed due for heavy rain.
The race was delayed due by heavy rain.
The race was delayed due of heavy rain.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase due to expresses the cause of the delay and is the only option that uses it correctly.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes a prescriptive style guide?
choices: It documents how writers use language in actual published work.
It tells writers which language choices to follow.
It identifies which grammar rules are difficult to learn.
It ranks writing styles from most to least formal.
questions.explanation: A prescriptive style guide tells writers which language choices to follow.

questions.prompt: Which sentence avoids a dangling participial modifier?
choices: Completing the route, Maya's map needed repair.
After completing the route, checking the map helped Maya.
After completing the route, Maya checked her map.
Completing the route, the map was checked by Maya.
questions.explanation: The subject of the introductory participial phrase, Maya, is also the subject of the main clause.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the past-tense form correctly in American English?
choices: She practised the violin yesterday.
She practiced the violin yesterday.
She practice the violin yesterday.
She practicing the violin yesterday.
questions.explanation: American English uses practiced as the past tense of practice, while practised is the usual British form.

questions.prompt: According to the AP Stylebook, which pronoun correctly completes this gender-neutral sentence? Each athlete packed ___ warm-up gear.
choices: their
theirs
them
his
questions.explanation: AP Stylebook permits singular they, so their is the correct gender-neutral possessive pronoun for the singular antecedent each athlete.

questions.prompt: A style guide recommends toward for the preposition meaning in the direction of. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The rider moved towards the gate.
The rider moved toward the gate.
The rider moved toword the gate.
The rider moved toward of the gate.
questions.explanation: The guide specifies toward, and this sentence uses that preposition without an extra word or a misspelling.

questions.prompt: A style guide recommends the order size, age, shape, color, origin, material, and purpose for adjectives. Which phrase follows that order?
choices: a blue small old car
a small old blue car
an old small blue car
a blue old small car
questions.explanation: The phrase a small old blue car follows the specified order of size, age, and color.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses subject-verb agreement correctly with the subject either of the two trails?
choices: Either of the two trails mark as closed.
Either of the two trails are marked as closed.
Either of the two trail is marked as closed.
Either of the two trails is marked as closed.
questions.explanation: The phrase either of the two trails is treated as a singular subject.

questions.prompt: According to the AP Stylebook, which sentence uses between correctly?
choices: The debate between the two classes was lively.
The debate among the two classes was lively.
The debate between the two class was lively.
The debate between two class was lively.
questions.explanation: AP style generally uses between for two distinct items and among for more than two, so the two classes belong with between.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the past-tense modal correctly?
choices: We should have known the answer.
We should of known the answer.
We should been knowing the answer.
We should knew the answer.
questions.explanation: The modal should is followed by have plus a past participle, so should have known is the standard past-tense construction.

questions.prompt: A style guide says to use fewer with countable nouns and less with uncountable nouns. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: There was fewer traffic on the road after the storm.
There were less traffic on the road after the storm.
There were fewer traffic on the road after the storm.
There was less traffic on the road after the storm.
questions.explanation: Traffic is an uncountable noun, so less is the correct comparative word in this sentence.

questions.prompt: A style guide says to use and with a comma when it joins two independent clauses to form a compound sentence. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The engine revved and the rider leaned into the turn.
The engine revved, the rider leaned into the turn.
The engine revved, and the rider leaned into the turn.
The engine revved; and the rider leaned into the turn.
questions.explanation: The option uses a comma before and to join two independent clauses, exactly as the guide requires.

questions.prompt: A style guide requires one space after the period at the end of a sentence. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The briefing ended.  The riders entered the course.
The briefing ended.The riders entered the course.
The briefing ended. The riders entered the course.
The briefing ended.  The riders prepared for the course.
questions.explanation: The sentence with one space after the period follows the guide's stated spacing rule.

questions.prompt: A school style guide recommends the wording student with a disability rather than disability student. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The student with disability requested a ramp.
The student with a disability requested a ramp.
The disabled student requested a ramp.
The disability student requested a ramp.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses the guide's preferred wording by identifying the person as a student with a disability.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly hyphenates the compound modifier?
choices: The lab bought a state of the art microscope.
The lab bought a states-of-the-art microscope.
The lab bought a state-of-art microscope.
The lab bought a state-of-the-art microscope.
questions.explanation: A state-of-the-art microscope uses hyphens to show that several words form one compound modifier before the noun.

questions.prompt: Which reason best explains why a professional style guide provides rules for disputed usages?
choices: To make recurring language choices consistent across a publication.
To remove every possible choice from an author's writing.
To declare every disputed practice permanently incorrect.
To make grammatical judgment unnecessary in edited prose.
questions.explanation: A style guide establishes consistent practices for recurring language choices while leaving room for context.
questions.skill: Explaining the purpose of style guides

questions.prompt: According to the MLA Handbook (9th ed.), how is a works-cited entry for a print book indented?
choices: The first line is indented 0.5 inch, and subsequent lines are flush left.
Every line is indented 0.5 inch.
The first line is flush left, and subsequent lines are indented 0.5 inch.
Every line is flush left with no indentation.
questions.explanation: MLA works-cited entries use a hanging indent, with the first line flush left and each later line indented 0.5 inch.

source.claim: The rule of using "whom" prescribes that it is used when it serves as the object of a verb or preposition, such as after "to".
source.quote: As a general rule, the subjective form is used when the pronoun is the subject of a verb, as in he kicked the ball , whereas the objective form is used as the direct or indirect object of a verb, or the object (complement) of a preposition . For example: Sue kicked him , someone gave him the ball , Mary was with him .

source.claim: A serial (Oxford) comma precedes the conjunction in a list of three or more items.
source.quote: The serial comma (also referred to as the Oxford comma or Harvard comma ) is a comma placed after the penultimate term in a list (just before the conjunction ) when writing out three or more terms. For example, a list of three countries might be punctuated with the serial comma as "France, Italy, and Spain" or without it as "France, Italy and Spain".
